Systems I built that moved real numbers

Built with minimal tech involvement. Each solves one expensive operational problem.

Flagship Build
AI Ticket-Triage & Verification Agent

Directed and personally built an AI agent that resolves Kiwi's Freshdesk support tickets end to end: pulls the ticket, cross-verifies the real root cause against live backend APIs, internal data warehouses, and payment-gateway records rather than trusting a single ledger snapshot, drafts a fully compliant customer reply, and routes genuine bugs to the right engineering owner. A human reviews and signs off before anything reaches a customer, by design, not as a limitation.

Self-corrects its own rules in place when one turns out wrong
What it's caught in production
False “confirmed bugs” stopped before escalation. A batch of tickets that read as confirmed backend issues from ledger data alone turned out, checked live, to be mostly unverifiable or already explained by policy. None were wrongly promised to a customer or filed to engineering.
Hidden reward exclusions surfaced. A “missing reward” that the ledger alone made look like a bug was actually a policy exclusion, and the same check caught a second exclusion on the account the customer hadn't even flagged.
Cross-ticket pattern detection. Two unrelated customers, weeks apart, hit the identical undocumented milestone-delay pattern, invisible to two agents working their own queues in isolation.
Self-corrects its own knowledge base. When a rule turned out wrong, such as a customer message wrongly assumed to be Kiwi-originated, it was corrected in place and explained, not just patched for one ticket.
Verifies every conclusion against live systems before a reply goes out. Human sign-off retained on every send.

More things I've built

GoKiwi's CS org runs on 12+ of these day to day — a working sample below, not the full list.

CS Weekly Reporting Engine
Two purpose-built weekly reports pulled from live data: one for founders on issues that persist week over week, one for ops on queue health, kept deliberately separate after merging them once produced misleading results.
Dobby Evals
An independent grading harness for the AI ticket-triage agent: re-derives ground truth from live systems rather than trusting the agent's own conclusions, and scores each run pass or fail across 5 dimensions.
CX Copilot
A SOP-grounded chat assistant for support agents: answers policy questions by pulling the right SOP and FAQ source live, with every query logged for latency and accuracy review.
Jira Status Dashboard & Alerts
A live Jira status dashboard plus scheduled email automation, sending daily and weekly ticket status to individual agents and a leadership alert list.
Card Closure Compliance Classifier
Resolves every card-closure request against live per-bank application status, classifying each as should-retain or should-not-retain per policy before a human opens the ticket.
AV3 Sweep
Bulk-processes an entire open ticket bucket in one pass: diagnoses root cause per user from live data, groups by verified cause, and drafts responses for approval.
Offline Dobby (R&D)
An experiment porting the ticket-triage agent to a fully local, offline model, to test whether an open-weight model could do the job without an API cost. Verdict: not yet, kept as exploratory, not shipped.

How I think about customer operations

Principles, not tactics. These guide every decision I make.

01
Automate repetitive work before hiring more people
Identify the 20% of issue types driving 80% of tickets. Automate those first. Headcount is a last resort, not a first response.
02
Fix root causes, not ticket volume
A rising queue is a product signal. I treat support as an insight engine and use it to push upstream fixes that eliminate contact entirely.
03
Use AI to reduce effort, not accountability
Deploy AI where answers are deterministic. Keep humans where judgment matters. Never use automation to avoid ownership.
04
Treat support as a strategic data source
Every ticket is signal. I build systems that surface patterns and translate them directly into product roadmap inputs, with evidence, not anecdote.
05
Measure every process by cost, speed, and impact
If I can't quantify it, I don't trust it. Metrics attached to every initiative from day one: CSAT delta, resolution time, deflection rate.
06
Build infrastructure that outlasts you
SOPs, QA frameworks, escalation paths: systems designed to run at quality regardless of who is on shift. Durability over dependency.
